summary.text: The rock cycle describes how the three main rock types, sedimentary, metamorphic and igneous, turn into one another over geologic time.
A rock changes when it is forced out of its equilibrium conditions, and, driven by plate tectonics and the water cycle, rocks keep changing as they meet new environments.
Any existing rock can be changed by metamorphism, and any of the three types can melt into magma and cool into igneous rock.

facts.label: Driving forces
facts.value: Plate tectonics and the water cycle

facts.label: Slow-cooled example
facts.value: Granite, coarse-grained, cooled inside the Earth

facts.label: Fast-cooled example
facts.value: Obsidian, a natural glass with no crystals

items.prompt: A block of basalt sits exposed to air and rain on a hillside for a very long time. What happens to it?

options.label: It stays the same, being already formed
It breaks down and parts of it dissolve
It turns into metamorphic rock where it sits
It slowly melts back into magma

items.explain: Rocks exposed to the atmosphere are unstable; weathering breaks them into fragments and carries away dissolved material.

items.prompt: Two rocks form from the same magma: one cools deep underground, the other cools on the surface. Which ends up with bigger crystals?

options.label: The one that cooled deep underground
The one that cooled on the surface
Both have exactly the same crystals
Neither has any crystals at all

items.explain: Rock cooling within the Earth cools very slowly and becomes coarse-grained, while rock cooling at the surface is fine-grained.

items.prompt: Sand grains worn off a granite are buried, compacted and fused together into solid rock. What kind of rock is it now?

options.label: Igneous, like the granite it came from
Metamorphic, because it was squeezed
Sedimentary, made of grains fused together
No type until it melts again

items.explain: A single grain still belongs to the rock class it came from, but a rock made of such grains fused together is sedimentary.

items.prompt: Which kinds of rock can melt into magma and later cool into igneous rock?

options.label: Only igneous rock itself
Only metamorphic rock
Only sedimentary rock
Any of the three types

items.explain: Igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks can all melt into magma and cool into igneous rocks.

items.prompt: Lava pours out of a volcano and cools so quickly that no crystals have time to grow. What forms?

options.label: A natural glass such as obsidian
A coarse rock such as granite
A layered rock such as sandstone
A banded rock such as gneiss

items.explain: Volcanic rock can cool so fast that no crystals form, leaving a natural glass like obsidian.

items.prompt: A body of magma pushes into older rock and heats the rock all around it. What process changes that surrounding rock?

options.label: Weathering and erosion
Metamorphism from the heat
Lithification of fragments
Deposition by rivers

items.explain: Rock touched by an igneous intrusion is altered and recrystallized by the magma's heat, which is contact metamorphism.
